text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers:

- Slovenia's Constitutional Court said on Thursday the country's constitution should be changed before the ratification of its association accord with the European Union in order to allow foreigners to buy real estate in Slovenia.
- The Slovenian government on Thursday sent a proposal to parliament to amend real estate legislation in line with EU standards as soon as possible.
- A new general agreement between workers, employers and the government on workers' social benefits is expected to be signed on Monday.
- Railway workers on Thursday decided to postpone their planned strike until Tuesday, when they expect to continue negotiations with their management.

- The Bank of Slovenia is expected to announce the completion of the rehabilitation programmes for Slovenia's two largest state owned banks, Nova Ljubljanska Banka and Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor, on Friday.
- Presidents of eight Central European countries will start their fourth two-day annual meeting in the coastal town of Portoroz on Friday.

- Some 45.8 percent of Slovenians believe the government should compromise with striking railway workers, while almost 32 percent think the government should stand firm in such cases, a poll conducted by the paper showed.
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Thursday he expected parliament to amend the nation's constitution in June to enable foreigners to buy real estate.
- Credit rating agency Dun & Bradstreet on Thursday awarded Slovenia an unchanged DB3a credit rating for June, placing it second in the region just behind the Czech Republic and ahead of Poland.
- Slovenian port operator Luka Koper said it will slash its 1996 dividend to 100 tolars ($0.64) from 202.5 tolars last year.
